events.title: A year in
events.from: Marianne Okafor, Chief Executive
events.body:
A year ago I gave you twenty-three minutes and asked for three risks. This time I have an hour and a different question: what will be true in December that is not true now, and what are you leaving alone to get it?

The committee has your review. So do I.

events.title: A fifth less, as agreed
events.from: Tomas Lindqvist, Chief Financial Officer
events.body: This year's plan went to the board with a fifth less for cyber, as you agreed in the autumn. That is the line you have. If the year asks for more, the conversation starts from what you said then.

events.title: The line held
events.from: Tomas Lindqvist, Chief Financial Officer
events.body: The cyber line held, on the argument you made in the autumn. I said I would hold you to it, so here it is in writing: in October I will ask what the money bought that a fifth less would not have.

events.title: The line you named
events.from: Tomas Lindqvist, Chief Financial Officer
events.body: The line you offered back has gone, and the rest of the cyber budget stands. It was the easiest conversation I had about this year's plan, because I could say what we were giving up.

events.title: Last year's emergency spend, paid
events.from: Tomas Lindqvist, Chief Financial Officer
events.body: Last year you committed money beyond the cyber line for emergency support. It has been paid, out of this year's line, which is smaller by that much. I am telling you so that nobody is surprised in March.

events.title: Your three risks, adopted
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: The committee adopted the three risks you named as this year's priorities. In July I will ask what has moved on each, and I will ask it in front of the CFO.

events.title: Your delivery plan, adopted
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: The committee adopted your delivery plan as this year's priorities. In July I will ask what each programme is for, in terms the committee can test rather than dates it can only note.

events.title: Your three questions, adopted
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: The committee adopted your three questions as this year's priorities, which is not something it has done before. In July I will ask which of them you can now answer, and how you know.

events.title: The priorities, at half-time
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: Half the year, and the committee has heard about its priorities in your papers this year. It can see what moved and what did not, which is what it asked for in January.

effectsOnReveal.reason: The committee heard about its priorities all year.

events.title: The priorities, unheard
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: Half the year, and the committee has heard little about the priorities it adopted from you in January. I would like that put right before October, in a paper rather than a corridor.

effectsOnReveal.reason: The committee heard little this year about the priorities it took from you.

events.title: Last year's acceptances still stand
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: Some of the risks you accepted last year are still accepted, to the dates you gave them: {{acceptedRisks}}. Anything you recorded as assumed in accepting them came across too. When each date arrives it will come back to you, as it would have in December.

events.title: A resignation after the winter
events.from: {{pressedLeader}}
events.body: Somebody in {{pressedFunction}} who carried last winter has resigned. The notice runs to the end of next month, and the post is not easy to fill. I would rather you heard it from me than from the vacancy list.

events.title: Everyone came back
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: Everyone who was here in December is here in January. That is less usual than it sounds after a year like the last one, and the team knows you noticed what it cost.

events.title: The Kestrel boundary, in January
events.from: Tomas Lindqvist, Chief Financial Officer
events.body: You held the Kestrel boundary through peak trading. It is the first week of January, as I said it would be, and the synergy number is still waiting on it.

events.title: Enforcement after peak
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: Enforcement was promised for after peak trading, and peak is over. The exception list grew by forty while we waited. I can switch enforcement on next week if you want it on.

events.title: A year of voluntary enrolment
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: The second factor has been voluntary since the autumn. The accounts that never enrolled are the accounts the alerts keep tracing back to, and the list of them is not getting shorter on its own.

events.title: The restore test, in January
events.from: Helen Brandt, Chief Operating Officer
events.body: You deferred the production restore test to January. It is January. I can give you four hours of payments on a Sunday morning this month; after that the window closes until the spring.

events.title: Corvus, on last year's paper
events.from: Nadia Farrell, Director of Procurement and Supplier Management
events.body: Corvus is in its first quarter on the contract you renewed unchanged. Its engineers still hold standing access, and the account list has grown by six since renewal. None of that breaches the contract, which is the point I would make about the contract.

events.title: Two providers, six weeks
events.from: Nadia Farrell, Director of Procurement and Supplier Management
events.body: The tender closed and the new provider starts in March. For six weeks both Corvus and its replacement will hold access while the handover runs, and Corvus has less reason than ever to be careful with it.

events.title: Corvus had to ask
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: Corvus needed emergency access at the weekend and, for the first time, had to ask for it. It took eleven minutes, it was logged, and it was closed when they were done. Schedule four did what it says.

events.title: The auditors start where they stopped
events.from: Tomas Lindqvist, Chief Financial Officer
events.body: The auditors are back in March for privileged access, and they are starting from the note they wrote in December: that management's account of the programme was ahead of production. They will test everything we say this time.

events.title: The regulator asks about last year
events.from: Ruth Ahmadi, General Counsel and Data Protection Officer
events.body: The regulator has written about last year's incidents. They want the post-incident review and evidence that its actions were completed, by the end of next month. What we send will be read alongside what we told them at the time.

events.title: An assistant on every desk
events.from: Helen Brandt, Chief Operating Officer
events.body: Customer service wants an AI assistant on every agent's desktop by the autumn. It reads the case history, the order record and the customer's messages, and drafts the reply. The supplier's terms say our data is not used to train their model. I would like your view before I sign.

events.title: A quarter into the second year
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: A quarter in. The committee knows you now, which changes what it will accept: less benefit of the doubt than last year, and less patience with surprises. It also listens more closely, which you can use.

events.title: Seventy-two hours
events.from: Ruth Ahmadi, General Counsel and Data Protection Officer
events.body: New rules come into force in October: a significant incident must be reported to the regulator within seventy-two hours of our knowing about it. Nobody is sure whose decision it is, so nobody can say how long one would take.

events.title: The last of the legacy data centre
events.from: Dev Raghunathan, Chief Information Officer
events.body: We can switch off the legacy data centre in October, as planned, if the systems still in it move or go. Two of them support despatch, and the people who understood them have left. I am not asking for anything yet; I am telling you where the risk will be in September.

events.title: Peak trading, again
events.from: Helen Brandt, Chief Operating Officer
events.body: Peak trading starts next month and the change freeze with it. Security changes are not automatically exempt this year either, but I will hear a case for any that cannot wait.

events.title: Your second year review
events.from: Marianne Okafor, Chief Executive
events.body: Your second year is nearly up. I will want to know what is true now that was not true last January, what you chose to leave alone, and what you would do with a third.

events.title: Nothing new until it lands
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: Holding new work back until what is running lands has done what you meant it to: the team has stopped switching between things. It has also meant saying no to two requests the CIO thought were small.

events.title: What the team year bought
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: The training budget has gone where you said it would, and the people who were close to leaving in December have stayed. The work has moved more slowly while we did it, and the executive has noticed that too.

events.title: What the assistant was told
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: An agent pasted a customer's full card number into the assistant to ask what it was. The supplier keeps prompts for thirty days for quality review, so that card number now sits in a log we do not control. It will not be the only one.

events.title: The assessment narrowed the assistant
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: The data protection assessment found the assistant could read closed-account records as well as live ones. The scope was narrowed before go-live, and the supplier's prompt log is now switched off for our tenancy.

events.title: What the pilot showed
events.from: Helen Brandt, Chief Operating Officer
events.body: The pilot team closed cases faster, and found two things nobody expected: the assistant quotes old refund policy, and agents paste in more than they need to. Both are fixable before the wider roll-out, which is now later than I wanted.

events.title: The regulator wants the whole review
events.from: Ruth Ahmadi, General Counsel and Data Protection Officer
events.body: The regulator has written back about the summary we sent. They would like the full post-incident review, and they asked, politely, why we chose to summarise it. I have no good answer to that second question.

effectsOnReveal.reason: The regulator asked for the review you had summarised.

events.title: Seventy-two hours, tested
events.from: Ruth Ahmadi, General Counsel and Data Protection Officer
events.body: We ran the new reporting process against an exercise incident. A decision in thirty-one hours, with the person who makes it named in advance. I would rather find that out in an exercise than in October.
